plan: With 3 bidders and uniform values on [0,49], the Bayesian-Nash equilibrium bid strategy for a first-price auction is to bid (n-1)/n times your value, which for n=3 gives 2/3 of value. My value is $9, so optimal bid ≈ $6.00. This balances winning probability against profit margin, avoiding overpaying while still competitive.

With 3 bidders and values uniform on [0,49], the symmetric Nash equilibrium bid function for a first-price auction is b(v) = v*(n-1)/n = v*(2/3). My value is $9, so optimal bid ≈ $6. This balances winning probability against profit margin, avoiding overpaying while still competing effectively against Andy and Charles.

With 3 bidders and independent uniform values on [0,49], the standard first-price auction equilibrium bid is value*(n-1)/n = 34*(2/3) ≈ 22.67. This balances the trade-off between winning probability and profit margin. Bidding my full value would give zero profit if I win, so shading is optimal. I'll bid close to this theoretical equilibrium to maximize expected profit while maintaining a reasonable chance of winning against Andy and Betty.
